test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Consider the below statements:

1. Governor is state's constitutional head.

2. He acts solely on Council's advice.

Which of teh above statements holds true regarding Governor's executive powers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state, as per Article 154 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in cases where he is empowered to act at his discretion.
 
• Discretionary powers of the Governor include reserving a bill for the consideration of the President and recommending President's rule under Article 356.
 
• Statement 2 is incorrect because the Governor does not act solely on the advice of the Council; he has discretionary powers in specific situations.
 
• Thus, only Statement 1 is correct regarding the Governor's executive powers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 154:** The executive power of the state is vested in the Governor and is exercised either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
 
• **Discretionary Powers:** The Governor can act independently in certain cases, such as appointing the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority.
 
• **Advice of Council of Ministers:** As per Article 163, the Governor is generally bound to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• **President’s Rule:** Under Article 356, the Governor can recommend President’s rule if the state government cannot function according to constitutional provisions.
 
• **Reservation of Bills:** The Governor can reserve bills for the President's consideration under Article 200, especially in matters affecting the central government or other constitutional issues.
